about.title: Gustine Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Gustine is a small town of about 5,756 people in Merced County, and most of what people here buy, drive, or work with was built somewhere else. When one of those products fails — a hitch that shears, a space heater that ignites, a child's car seat that unlatches on Rt 33 — the harm lands locally even though the responsibility sits with a manufacturer far away. California law accounts for that gap. Under strict product liability, you generally do not have to prove the company was careless. You need to show the product had a defect in its design, its manufacturing, or its warnings, and that the defect caused your injury. That is a lighter burden than a standard negligence claim. We are a product liability team that handles defective-product cases on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. Keep the product, the packaging, and any receipts. Those items often decide the case.

whyChoose.title: Why Gustine Residents Choose Us for Product Cases

items.title: Strict liability changes the question
items.desc: In California you usually don't have to prove the manufacturer was negligent — only that the product was defective and that the defect hurt you. Our team understands that distinction and can frame your claim the right way from day one.

items.title: More than one company may owe you
items.desc: The maker, the distributor, and the store that sold the product can each be held responsible under California law. We can sort out who belongs in the claim so nothing is left on the table.

items.title: Preserving the evidence, starting now
items.desc: The product itself is the heart of a defect case, and we can help arrange for it to be kept safe and examined before it's thrown out or repaired. We work on contingency, with no fee unless you recover.

items.question: I was in a crash on Rt 140 near Gustine and I think the airbag or tires failed. Is that a product case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It can be both. Gustine recorded 8 injury collisions in 2025, and when a vehicle component fails during a crash, the injured person may have a strict liability claim against the part's manufacturer alongside any claim against another driver. Don't let the vehicle be scrapped or repaired until an attorney has looked at it, because the damaged part is the proof.

items.question: Do I really have to prove the company did something wrong?
items.answer: Usually not. California's strict liability rule means you generally only need to show the product was defective — in its design, how it was made, or the warnings that came with it — and that the defect caused your injury. Whether the company was careful or careless is often beside the point.

items.question: I threw away the box and don't have the receipt. Can I still make a claim?
items.answer: Possibly, yes. The product itself matters most, so keep it exactly as it is and don't try to fix it. Bank statements, order confirmations, photos, and medical records can help fill in gaps, and our team can advise on what to gather next.
